newsitem.title: CANADA: Teen-agers will not be charged in cult deaths.
newsitem.headline: Teen-agers will not be charged in cult deaths.

text.p: Canadian prosecutors said on Thursday no criminal charges would be laid against three teen-agers whose parents died in a group suicide by five members of the Solar Temple cult in Quebec last month.
Prosecutor Mario Tremblay told a news conference in Quebec City that investigators found no evidence that the teen-agers' actions had contributed in a criminal way to the deaths.

Police at one stage had questioned whether the teenagers might have assisted in setting the house fire which killed the five adults, all French citizens, in the village of Saint-Casimir near Quebec City on March 22.

"Considering the frankly exceptional circumstances of this affair, and the age of the adolescents, there is good reason to wonder about responsibility, to the point where I believe that no jury or judge...would hold them responsible," said Tremblay.
The children, aged 13, 14, and 16, were not injured in the blaze, which was started by a crude incendiary device made from propane tanks and an electric burner.
Tremblay said that on several occasions, the children had attempted to stop their parents, Didier Queze, 39, his wife Chantal Goupillot-Queze, 41, and the other three adults from committing suicide.
The adults made three failed attempts over 48 hours before succeeding in setting the fire.
The victims, who all died of asphyxiation, were members of the Solar Temple, a doomsday cult whose members believe a ritualized death takes them on a journey to a new life on the star Sirius.
Including the Saint-Casimir deaths, 74 cult members and others have been killed in group suicides and murders in Quebec, France and Switzerland since October 1994.
